founder.description: The org's founding member; sponsor of the invite and the only checkpointer in this workflow.

joiner.description: The invited member, on a machine with its own personal fleet.

adopted_checkpoint.description: The actor's adopted-checkpoint cache holds a checkpoint including the joiner (adopted_checkpoint_founder, adopted_checkpoint_joiner).

bootstrap_snapshot.description: The founder's ledger events, binding and profiles as of the bootstrap moment.

checkpoint_delegate_grant.description: A hot delegate grant whose scope includes signing advancing checkpoints.
checkpoint_delegate_grant.store: founder's org ledger and audited vault

checkpoint_including_joiner.description: A registry checkpoint seq n+1 whose members_root includes the joiner (checkpoint_seq_n).

checkpoint_seed.description: Registry membership checkpoint seq 0, signed by the org root.

claim_approval.description: The founder's countersignature on a staged claim.

delegate_grant.description: The actor's storage delegate event, persona-signed, parents = local heads.
delegate_grant.notes: Not read by _sync_org_peers; whether a pull needs it is unproven.
delegate_grant.store: the actor's org ledger and audited vault

fleet_roster.description: A personal fleet roster entry for the actor's machine; required by the runtime mint (fleet_enrollment_routes.py:_runtime_context).
fleet_roster.notes: For a fresh joiner with no personal fleet, unverified (graph://cde6c8c6-041 §1 J6).

install_seed_addresses.defect: graph://cde6c8c6-041 §5 J5 reachability seed: network-join.js:313-327 does not forward reachability_rows
install_seed_addresses.description: Co-member addresses in the joiner's install seed.
install_seed_addresses.notes: No built producer; the join page does not forward reachability_rows (network-join.js:313-327).

invite_ref_resolved.description: {org, invite_ref} resolved from the registry envelope of the link.

join_context.description: The claim context served by the founder's connector (genesis_id, heads, granted_role, binding, sponsor).

join_link_grant.description: The org:join grant row, the relay link and the stored invite bearer.

ledger_heads.description: The actor's copy of the org ledger and its current heads (founder_heads, joiner_heads).
ledger_heads.store: autonomy.org.ledger-event#1 rows in the org DB

link_publish_approval.description: The approved link_publish decision with its Gate 2 org-scoped sign-on.

member_admitted.description: The claim appended to the founder's ledger.

member_claim_final.description: The claim re-minted at the pinned position carrying the approvals.

persona_cert_fleet_sync.description: The org sync certificate (persona -> serving machine key, scope fleet:sync) with its serving seed, installed as an OrgFleetAuthenticator.

policy_approval.description: The invite's role requires approvals before admission.

policy_self_admit.description: The invite's role admits a claim without approvals.

reachability_row.description: The actor machine's signed reachability row in the org scope.
reachability_row.home: the actor's machine; co-members after a pull
reachability_row.store: org scope Settings, replicated by org sync

registered_serving_key.description: The actor's serving machine key in the registry's per-org serve_machine_keys allow-set.
registered_serving_key.notes: Enforced only when the set is non-empty (relay.py:973-1000, store.py:1576-1583); the only writer in the tree is this backfill. Whether any live org's set is non-empty is an open question; the goal does not require it.

registry_binding.description: The org's registry binding {org_uuid, root key, registry_url}.

relay_slot.description: A live serving slot of the actor's connector at the org's relay.

serve_cert.description: The actor's persona-signed serving certificate and key.
serve_cert.store: autonomy.machine.serve-cert row; serving key in autonomy.machine.vault.audited

org_sync_pull.description: Founder and joiner can each pull the other over org sync: both hold an org channel (sync certificate + serving seed), both have adopted a checkpoint whose members_root includes the joiner (the verifier admits a pull only under an adopted seq with inclusion, fleet_org_channel.py: 286-309), the joiner holds the org ledger, and the joiner has a route to the founder (the founder reaches the joiner through its dial-in).
org_sync_pull.notes: Peer selection sources (fleet_sync_scheduler.py:_org_peer_candidates): reachability rows (need a prior pull), install seed, relay slots through the dialer's own connector, dialed-in peers. The founder-pulls-joiner direction riding the joiner's dial-in is taken from the record, not re-traced. The single-joiner AND/OR graph cannot express head presence at adoption; OrgAdmission.tla carries that.

approval.description: Founded org (F0 done), invite role requires the founder's approval.

self_admit.description: Founded org (F0 done), invite role self-admits.

custody.forced_by: Operator-approved encrypted retention in personal-homed audited Settings, replicated across the member's fleet. Opened on demand, with no separate signing-key cache. Authority stays scope-attenuated, TTL-bounded and fold-enforced.

descriptor.bound: The delegating persona's own membership; the fold rejects any overreach.
descriptor.live: Yes — records must reach honest nodes, which verify them against the fold.
descriptor.reaches: Exactly two execution scopes, storage:state:advance and storage:capability:grant, and nothing else. It signs; it opens nothing. It authorizes only by resolving its delegation chain to a member persona: a chain terminating outside the member roster is void, and generic scope-holding is never consulted for these two scopes.
descriptor.revoke: Delegation revocation and ninety-day expiry. Sign-in reuses with at least thirty days remaining; otherwise mints a new keypair and grant.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing.

agent_delegate_signing_key.notes: graph://b437ecfb-e23 governs retention. Public metadata is keyed by genesis in autonomy.network.storage-delegate. A reuse sign-in writes no delegation event; no scheduled renewal runs. This is storage-ledger authority, not generic Settings row-signing authority.

custody.forced_by: Persisted in the browser's IndexedDB and usable with no further human interaction until its certificate expires; theft through the page is prevented by WebCrypto non-extractability, and the bound is the certificate validity window plus revocation.

descriptor.bound: The certificate's validity window and scope list.
descriptor.live: Yes — its signatures must reach the dashboard or registry.
descriptor.reaches: The scopes its persona-signed delegation certificate carries (SESSION_SCOPES in network-signon.mjs): delegate:agent, link:publish, link:revoke, tunnel:serve, turn:allocate, and viewer:identify — one certificate per organization persona, all over the single session key.
descriptor.revoke: The certificate validity window (default twenty-four hours, maximum thirty days), enforced at load and by an expiry watchdog that signs the browser out; a root-signed revocation record is the explicit path. Not a ceremony.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing through the page: the key is created extractable:false and _installSession refuses any key claiming otherwise, so no script can export it; it appears in no replicated store.

browser_session_key.notes: Minted per browser during the sign-on ceremony, after the user proves root authority by satisfying the armor's factor policy; routine operations then sign with crypto.subtle.sign and never see a factor again during the certificate's validity. Distinct from the per-operation vault authorize ceremony, which costs one user-verified assertion per class open and involves no session key.
signs: registry request envelopes only (REQUEST_DOMAIN + canonical JSON of v, method, path, ts, signer, payload) — the single crypto.subtle.sign call site for this key in network-signon.mjs

custody.forced_by: Released only inside a factor ceremony and never across the release boundary — exporting it would release the whole class.

descriptor.bound: The class's membership at each generation.
descriptor.reaches: Every content key sealed under that class generation.
descriptor.revoke: Factor revocation appends the next generation sealed to the survivors and the anchor; it applies at the next write and touches no existing sealed material.
descriptor.snapshot: The class's secrets for generations this key belongs to.

custody.forced_by: Private recipient warms at root unlock for unattended audited reads.

descriptor.bound: Audited envelopes addressed to this recipient, not secured policy classes.
descriptor.live: No — possession of the private key and an envelope permits opening.
descriptor.reaches: Audited personal-vault object content keys sealed to this recipient.
descriptor.revoke: Replacement protects newly sealed material; follows personal-root lifecycle.
descriptor.snapshot: Opens retained audited envelopes sealed to this recipient.

delegate_audited_recipient.notes: X25519 encapsulation key, never a signing key. The public half supports cold writes. Organization isolation of personal-homed audited rows is enforced separately at the API namespace boundary; this derivation itself has no organization input.

custody.forced_by: Derived from an opened factor seed during access-only authentication; not retained for unattended operation.

descriptor.bound: Factor identity, single-use challenge and origin.
descriptor.live: Yes — a fresh server challenge and enrolled access policy are required.
descriptor.reaches: Proves an enrolled factor's dashboard access authority without opening the root.
descriptor.revoke: Removing the factor's access authority prevents further accepted proofs.
descriptor.snapshot: Access proof authority for that factor, not the root or organization content keys.

factor_access_signing_key.notes: Ed25519; HKDF purpose includes a terminal newline. Proof domain is autonomy.identity.factor-access-unlock.v1 followed by a newline and canonical challenge fields. Distinct from the X25519 factor recipient.

custody.forced_by: Re-derivable only from the cold factor seed.

descriptor.reaches: The policy shares sealed to it inside the armor envelope.
descriptor.revoke: Factor revocation; the envelope is re-signed without the share.
descriptor.snapshot: Those shares; the policy expression decides what they combine to.

custody.forced_by: Producing it requires the human gesture — typing the password or a passkey PRF assertion (crib Q0).

descriptor.reaches: The factor's derived recipient (its share of the root factor policy) and its derived dashboard access key. Only a factor set satisfying the policy expression reaches the root; unlock-only factors never do.
descriptor.revoke: Factor revocation re-signs the armor envelope without it.
descriptor.snapshot: That factor's policy shares. Whether the root follows depends on the policy expression, not on this key alone.

custody.forced_by: Root-derived at sign-in; private runtime retention uses RAM-backed carriers, not durable Settings.

descriptor.bound: Machine identity; reachability scopes node:announce and node:lookup.
descriptor.live: Yes — roster and certificate acceptance are authority boundaries.
descriptor.reaches: Signs fleet process delegations and registered personal-org reachability requests.
descriptor.revoke: Accepted roster removal and reachability certificate expiry.
descriptor.snapshot: No content decryption; possession supplies machine signing authority.

fleet_operating_signing_key.notes: Sync-only handoff omits this private seed. Registered personal-org handoff includes machine_private_seed and a root-direct reachability certificate (seven-day default). The browser checks the derived public half against roster machine_pub. This is not a KEM recipient.

custody.forced_by: Fresh runtime seed retained in process and RAM-backed warm carriers.

descriptor.bound: personal:<root-public-key> scope and named machine subject.
descriptor.live: Yes — runtime validates the live roster and delegation.
descriptor.reaches: Fleet synchronization under a machine-signed fleet:sync delegation.
descriptor.revoke: Roster removal or delegation expiry; maximum thirty-day lifetime.
descriptor.snapshot: No content decryption; permits synchronization within accepted scope.

fleet_process_signing_key.notes: Random Ed25519 process_private_seed, distinct from the operating key that signs its delegation.

custody.forced_by: Snapshot is total for its branch, offline.

descriptor.reaches: Every object under the generation and every ancestor via bridges.
descriptor.revoke: None — a generation secret is never retired.
descriptor.snapshot: Total for that branch, offline.

custody.forced_by: Subkeys of the sealed index; neither exists outside a release.

descriptor.reaches: K_index computes blind row addresses; K_meta seals row values. The blind index is the item-to-row mapping; nothing stores it.
descriptor.revoke: Follows the sealed index.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing — they are never at rest.

custody.forced_by: Encrypted organization-homed audited Setting replicated with organization content.

descriptor.bound: One link keypair and fragment trust anchor.
descriptor.live: Yes — viewer verifies against the public key in its URL fragment.
descriptor.reaches: Signs the serving handshake for one content share link.
descriptor.revoke: Active-grant checks stop future release; vaulted seed deletion does not erase delivered copies.
descriptor.snapshot: Proves possession for that link; cannot decrypt the organization vault or confer membership.

link_channel_signing_key.notes: graph://807b4e11-3e9. Random Ed25519 minted at publication, not sign-in. Seed lives in autonomy.network.link-channel-key; channel_pub is on the grant and projected into copied URL fragments. Dashboard opens it per viewer OPEN and gives only this key to the connector, never the org KEM. Content failures close the channel. Organization invitations use this same endpoint-authentication key alongside a separate claim bearer.

custody.forced_by: Derived only from the cold recovery code.

descriptor.bound: The one act; the fold rejects everything else.
descriptor.live: Yes — the rekey event must reach the ledger fold.
descriptor.reaches: Exactly one act: the recovery-authorized door of member.rekey. The genesis_id in the derivation keeps an identical printed code from linking personas across organizations.
descriptor.revoke: Enrolled at member.claim; changing it requires the current member recovery key or the org root. No event adds one after member.claim.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing — no plaintext, no content, no authority beyond the one door.

custody.forced_by: Unique per immutable revision and encrypts nothing else, so releasing it equals releasing that one plaintext — it is the unit allowed across the release boundary.

descriptor.reaches: One object revision's plaintext.
descriptor.revoke: Never — the revision is immutable; withdrawal is a new key for new writes.
descriptor.snapshot: That one revision.

custody.forced_by: Re-derivable from the generation secret during the warm period.

descriptor.reaches: One object revision's wrapped content key.
descriptor.revoke: Follows the generation secret; never individually retired.
descriptor.snapshot: That revision, given the ciphertext.

custody.forced_by: Constitutional acts are intent acts (crib Q0).

descriptor.live: Yes — it must reach the ledger or registry to be used.
descriptor.reaches: Genesis, key rotation, serve-certificate minting, registration, and rebind. It is not a domain principal: it holds no KEM credential and receives no capability grants.
descriptor.revoke: Org-vouch or dual-signed org-root rotation; both are ceremonies.
descriptor.snapshot: No content.

custody.forced_by: An audited vault setting: released unattended once the vault is open; encrypted at rest so a cold dump cannot run the offline location oracle.

descriptor.bound: One scope's location secrecy only; contents keep their own seals.
descriptor.reaches: Store row addresses within one scope (location, not content). Operator-personal and each organization scope have separate peppers.
descriptor.revoke: Requires re-addressing the affected scope's stores; normal get-or-create preserves the pepper.
descriptor.snapshot: Encrypted at rest, nothing. Held warm, the ability to test password guesses against vault locations offline.

custody.forced_by: The private half derives from the credential's PRF output on-device; using it requires a user-verified assertion at that machine.

descriptor.live: Yes — opening a seal needs the assertion at that machine.
descriptor.reaches: Payloads sealed to the credential's device. The public key is valid only when carried in a root-signed enrollment statement, verified before any seal is addressed to it.
descriptor.revoke: Passkey revocation (root-signed RevocationRecord).
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing without the device's PRF assertion.

custody.forced_by: Derived from the personal root at unlock and never persisted — the machine stores only its public machine_id; the key exists for the warm period and a reboot always waits on a human unlock.

descriptor.live: Yes — the thief must still be in the fleet and reachable.
descriptor.reaches: Distributions sealed to it after the theft — future persona KEM keys.
descriptor.revoke: Remove the machine from the fleet. Root-signed, not a ceremony.
descriptor.snapshot: Zero. It decrypts no existing record.

per_machine_key.notes: Designed KEM recipient only; concrete recipient derivation remains part of fleet.distribute_kem. The implemented Ed25519 key is fleet_operating_signing_key. Authentication and roster replication do not implement KEM distribution.

custody.forced_by: Snapshot is total: this key plus a copy of the replicated store is the whole domain history, offline. Not disk-eligible at any price.

descriptor.bound: None — damage is complete at the instant of theft.
descriptor.reaches: Every capability grant addressed to this persona, hence any head secret, hence all domain content including full history through the bridges.
descriptor.revoke: Publish a superseding PersonaKemCredential. Stops future grants only; undoes nothing already opened.
descriptor.snapshot: Total for the domain — key plus store copy is the whole history.

persona_kem_private.notes: Initial founding and admission derive counter zero, then bind the pair with kem_purpose(genesis_id). PersonaKemCredential has no counter field. Personal and organization sign-in handoffs open existing grants and keep KEM keys in process memory. Organization reads open late grants, and graceful reload uses the existing RAM-backed carrier to retain KEM keys, not generation secrets (graph://35308bf7-584, auto-a1pub). This key is not stored in audited Settings; cold restart needs sign-in.

custody.forced_by: Deriving it requires the personal root seed.

descriptor.live: Yes — records must reach honest nodes.
descriptor.reaches: Authorship of the persona's ledger events and key-control records in one organization. The genesis_id input keeps personas unlinkable across organizations.
descriptor.revoke: member.rekey moves the persona to a new key.
descriptor.snapshot: Authority to sign as the persona until rekeyed away.

custody.forced_by: Every act needing it expresses human intent (crib Q0), and its snapshot is total; no execution-class question is reached.

descriptor.reaches: Every purpose key ever derivable from it, and every vault policy class through each class's root-anchor wrap. Root authority reconstitutes the whole identity.
descriptor.revoke: None. The remedy is personal-root rotation, which requires the old root, the new root, and the enrolled recovery key (make_rotation in tools/network/idkit/root_rotation.py).
descriptor.snapshot: Total and unbounded, across every organization.

custody.forced_by: Its whole security property is being disjoint from the hot path; it is printed once and never touches a machine except in a recovery ceremony.

descriptor.reaches: Three domain-separated derivations, none reaching another: the armor recovery slot recipient, the recovery signing key, and the per-organization member recovery keys. The armor recipient opens the matching recovery slot, restoring personal-root authority.
descriptor.revoke: Replacement with the code in hand runs replace_recovery_slot (tools/network/idkit/root_factor_policy.py). Regeneration with the code lost is the witnessed succession window: declaration, blocking alert, cancellation or veto, completion after the window.
descriptor.snapshot: With the matching encrypted recovery record, restores the personal root and its downstream authority. This is the intentional master recovery capability, independent of the normal factor policy.

recovery_code.notes: One cold code supplies decryption and signing functions. The separate recovery signature prevents a hot-root thief without the cold code from rotating the identity. It does not prevent the code holder from recovering. Ordinary complete-authority rotation and the designed lost-code witnessed succession path are distinct workflows.

custody.forced_by: Derived only from the cold recovery code.

descriptor.live: Yes — its signatures must reach a verifier.
descriptor.reaches: The recovery co-signature on personal-root rotation and on recovery-code succession declarations.
descriptor.revoke: Recovery-code succession (the witnessed window).
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing; it signs and never decrypts.

custody.forced_by: Derived only from the cold recovery code.

descriptor.reaches: The root seed sealed into the armor's recovery slot.
descriptor.revoke: replace_recovery_slot re-seals the slot to a new code's recipient.
descriptor.snapshot: The sealed root seed, and nothing else.

custody.forced_by: Sealed to a root-derived recipient; opening it requires root authority.

descriptor.bound: None — it is the root's guaranteed floor under every class.
descriptor.reaches: Every vault policy class, through each class generation's mandatory anchor wrap — the indirection that lets root-factor churn touch only the armor.
descriptor.revoke: Irrevocable by design: revoke_factor refuses to drop it and the store refuses to persist a class generation without it.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing while sealed; every class once the root is open.

custody.forced_by: Exists only in sealed form; released by a factor ceremony.

descriptor.reaches: A sealed store's entire index — its address key and value key derive from it.
descriptor.revoke: Re-mint the store under a new index.
descriptor.snapshot: Nothing while sealed; the store's item map once released.

custody.forced_by: Vault-held since 2026-09-20 (graph://67d0aa5f-885 D4): a row of the machine-homed audited set autonomy.machine.vault.audited, sealed cold to the operator's audited delegate recipient, opened unattended once the vault is warm and released into ramfs for the connector at launch; never a disk file, never replicated. No content decryption; the serving child has bounded certificate scopes enforced by its relying parties.

descriptor.reaches: Authentication through tunnel:serve and serve:dns-01 certificates over the same serving child.
descriptor.revoke: Re-mint; thirty-day TTL, renewal below twenty days remaining.
descriptor.snapshot: No content decryption; possession permits use of accepted certificate scopes.

serving_delegate_key.notes: Organization registry and DNS01 certificates are persona-signed, not org-root-signed. No content viewer certificate is minted. The certificates live in the machine-homed autonomy.machine.serve-cert row keyed by org_uuid; the organization-homed autonomy.network.serve-cert set is deprecated.

custody.forced_by: Derived at root unlock for unattended serving; not stored separately.

serving_machine_signing_key.notes: Distinct from the personal fleet operating key and the serving delegate. Binding both organization and machine avoids presenting the same machine public key across organizations.

Recorded 2026-09-20 after the three certificates were found absent from this registry (keyreg-forensics.md, session auto-0919-212441).

fold.checkpoint.notes: Checkpoint is decided-removed from the design vocabulary; the handler remains in code, so it remains in this inventory.

preconditions: The delegated scope set never exceeds the delegator's (no scope escalation).

A revoked key cannot self-authorize its own rekey.
The new key proves control through the continuity signature.
Under recovery policy none, a recovery-authorized rekey is refused, never ignored.

module.org_reachability_publish.notes: A co-member reads the row only after a pull, so it cannot seed a first contact.

preconditions: Completion requires the elapsed witness window over a chain containing the declaration and no cancellation and no veto.

rekey.frontier_marker.notes: Without the marker the re-key achieves nothing (the F-001 defect); the calibration theory VaultRekeyF001 demonstrates exactly that.

root.rotation.notes: A local verification has no relying party (crib section 0: the owner rewriting their own store is a feature); the load-bearing checks are the registry rebind gate (tools/network/registry/app.py, which resolves the pinned recovery key server-side) and the fleet's root-signed RosterEntry acceptance (tools/network/fleet_roster.py).
preconditions: Three signatures — old root, enrolled recovery key, and new root. The succession convinces its relying parties, not the local machine - the fleet accepts a successor only against root-signed RosterEntry material, and the auto.network registry rebinds only for a request signed by the recovery key it pinned at enrollment.

writes: the staged claim appended with the approval

route.admit_on_approval.notes: Proposed consolidation F3+F4 (graph://cde6c8c6-041 §5): admission at countersign, so the checkpoint can run in the same window. Not built.

authority: registry membership state; this node's own ledger
route.checkpoint_adopt.notes: Never signs (docstring, network_routes.py:724-733). Callers: join install (:945), sign-on preparation (signon_preparation.py:140), and the route POST /api/network/membership-checkpoint/adopt; no background caller. The head-presence precondition is not monotone and is not expressed in requires; OrgAdmission.tla models it.
preconditions: Skip when the cached seq >= the registry seq (network_routes.py:756-758).

Fold the local ledger at the registry's ledger_head and require members_root equality; an id the local ledger lacks raises in ancestry/get and nothing is adopted (network_routes.py:759-768, fold.py:499-500, ledger.py:36-42, 66-77).
refusals: head absent from the local ledger

route.join_install.notes: Step J5. Does not produce install_seed_addresses: network-join.js (installAdmitted, :313-327) does not forward reachability_rows although the route reads them (network_routes.py:938-943). Deferred here (:804-805): storage delegate, serve cert, fleet runtime, sync cert.

autonomy.identity.machine.v1.description: Derives the per-machine operating key from the personal root seed and machine_id.

autonomy.identity.persona.v1.description: Derives a persona keypair from the personal root seed and genesis_id.

autonomy.identity.serving-machine.v1.description: Derives the organization-and-machine-specific Ed25519 serving key.

autonomy.network.ledger.sync-key.v1.description: Derives the ledger bundle sync key.

autonomy.recovery.kek.v1.description: Derives the recovery share of the master key-encryption key from the recovery code.

autonomy.recovery.member-sign.v1.description: Derives a per-organization member recovery key from the recovery code and genesis_id.

autonomy.recovery.signing.v1.description: Derives the recovery signing key from the recovery code.

autonomy/capability-grant/v1.description: Seals a generation secret to a PersonaKemCredential in a CapabilityGrant.

autonomy/object-wrap/v1.description: Derives an object revision's wrap key from its generation secret.

autonomy/personal-owner-at-rest/v1.description: Seals the personal owner key at rest.

autonomy/personal-vault/no-storage-gener.description: Domain label for personal vault objects outside any storage generation.

autonomy/personal-vault/revision-id/v1.description: Derives a personal vault object's revision identifier.

autonomy/receipt-pok/v1.description: Derives a CapabilityReceipt's proof-of-knowledge value from the state secret.

autonomy/recovery-armor/v1.description: Derives the recovery code's armor-slot recipient.

autonomy/root-factor-recipient/v1.description: Derives a factor's armor recipient from its factor seed.

autonomy/root-policy-wrap/v1.description: Wraps root-factor-policy node secrets inside the armor envelope.

autonomy/storage-domain/v1.description: Domain label for storage-domain identifiers in ledger projections.

autonomy/storage-parent-edge/v1.description: Keys a ParentBridge's child-to-parent generation recovery.

autonomy/storage-state-secret/v1.description: Domain label for generation-secret material in a StorageStateDescriptor.

autonomy/vault-factor/v1.description: Derives a factor's vault recipient inside the armor (distinct from the root-factor purpose).

autonomy/vault-policy-class/cek/v1.description: Wraps an object content key under a class generation.

autonomy/vault-policy-class/v1.description: Domain label for a vault policy class record.

autonomy/vault-policy-recipient/v1.description: Derives a factor's vault policy-class recipient from its factor seed.

autonomy/vault-root-anchor-wrap/v1.description: Wraps a class key to the root anchor's derived recipient.

autonomy/vault/delegate-audited-cek/v1.description: Seals an audited content key to the delegate recipient, bound to object and revision.

autonomy/vault/delegate-audited-recipien.description: Derives the dedicated X25519 recipient for unattended audited reads.

autonomy/vault/object-id/v1.description: Derives a vault storage object's identifier.

autonomy/vault/revision-id/v1.description: Derives a vault storage object's revision identifier.
